what: Exagamglogene autotemcel (exa-cel, Casgevy): CRISPR-Cas9 edit of the BCL11A +58 erythroid enhancer in a patient's own blood stem cells, for sickle cell disease.

approved.note: the first CRISPR therapy approved anywhere

target.motif: a GATA1 binding site at the core of that enhancer
target.why: BCL11A is the repressor that switches the gamma-globin genes off after birth. The +58 enhancer is what drives BCL11A in red-cell precursors and nowhere else, so breaking it lowers BCL11A in those cells only.
target.repair: Cas9 cuts both strands; the cell rejoins the ends by non-homologous end joining, which leaves small insertions or deletions that break the motif.

trial.name: CLIMB SCD-121
trial.source: Frangoul et al., N Engl J Med 2024;390:1649-1662

caveat: One infusion, after chemotherapy that clears the patient's own marrow. The edit is made outside the body in the patient's stem cells, and is not inherited.
